extracted.intended_audience: professional scientists and researchers in astronomy, physics, chemistry and photographic science (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing experimental and theoretical work in physical sciences (astronomy, physics, chemistry, photographic technique), including clarity of definitions, experimental protocol, interpretation of results, and suitability of proposed further work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a signal in mechanical/relativistic thought-experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion of an intersection point (e.g. point X where two sliding triangles meet) is not necessarily a 'signal' — the time of signalling from A to B must be reckoned from the moment A gives the impulse to the mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the physical propagation of impulses through materials (elastic wave speed) rather than treating geometric point motion as information transfer. Beware of treating instantaneous motion of constructed points as evidence of superluminal signalling; determine when a moving point corresponds to a physical carrier or merely a geometric locus.

rubrics_metrics.name: What counts as a satisfactory explanation of an anticyclone
rubrics_metrics.description: A meteorological explanation must account for why excess mass of air over an anticyclonic area does not 'roll off' and must explain how the geostrophic wind surrounding the anticyclone is produced and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rest on the simplistic statement that 'anticyclone = cold heavy air'. A robust account should explain the origin of the containing winds (geostrophic balance), the mechanism that produces them, and how they prevent the excess air from dispersing. Explanations that ignore production and maintenance of the wind are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum relevance for medical zoology
rubrics_metrics.description: Biology taught to medical students should focus on parts of zoology directly useful to them as anatomists or medical practitioners, rather than on remote descriptive facts about obscure animal types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing syllabi, prioritize material with clear clinical or anatomical relevance. Avoid including taxa or topics (e.g., sea-urchin vascular systems, leech digestive systems, bones of cod's head) that cannot be justified as directly useful within the time constraints of medical training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desensitiser efficacy for silver bromide–gelatin photographic plates
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical desensitiser must reduce plate sensitivity sufficiently to permit development in ordinary (fair) light without producing fogging; efficacy is measurable as the multiplicative reduction in sensitivity (examples: Phenosafranine ~40× reduction; certain dyes reduce 6–16×).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report quantitative reduction in sensitivity (fold-change) and the conditions used (concentration, immersion time). Demonstrate that desensitisation is sufficient for the intended working light (e.g., yellow light) and for plate types including orthochromatic and panchromatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectral-range performance of desensitisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Desensitisers vary in spectral effect (e.g., most marked loss in yellow/green; some dyes act strongly for blue rays but less so elsewhere); a useful desensitiser should operate over the spectral regions needed for the plate type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess desensitiser action across the spectrum relevant to the plate (blue, green, yellow, red, violet). Note that some dyes (Phenosafranine, Neutral Red) have broad action that is not simply correlated with their visible absorption; test empirically per plate halide composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staining and removability as a criterion of desensitisers
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical desensitisers should not cause persistent staining of the gelatin, celluloid, or skin, or should be removable by reasonable washing; staining properties limit practical utility (Phenosafranine stains strongly; Pinakryptol claimed to be non-staining).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and report whether the desensitiser leaves residues after normal washing, whether it stains handling surfaces or skin, and whether removal requires prolonged washing that might damage the emulsion or be impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical stability and developer compatibility of desensitisers
rubrics_metrics.description: The desensitising effect and practical use depend on developer composition and oxidation behaviour (e.g., omission of sulphite increases desensitising action because developers oxidize in air); instability or rapid oxidation of solutions is a drawback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report developer formulation and storage/stability issues. Test whether the desensitising agent or its oxidation products persist, change with time, or depend on presence/absence of anti-oxidants (sulphite). Consider whether the desensitising action stems from the dye or an oxidation product and whether that product adsorbs irreversibly to silver halide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between chemical structure and desensitising action
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain structural features (e.g., amino groups on safranines) influence desensitising power, but there is no simple constitutional rule — closely related dye families may differ sharply in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing new desensitisers, test structural analogues and report which functional groups correlate with activity. Describe anti-examples (aposafranine, safranones, safranol show reduced or no action) and note that unrelated dyes may nonetheless show weak desensitising properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental protocol recommendations for studying penetrating atmospheric/celestial radiations
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the origin and properties of penetrating radiations (ultra-X, corpuscular rays) investigators should repeat ionisation measurements at multiple locations and extend measurements to the highest altitudes attainable (balloons), coordinating internationally due to cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies to measure ionisation vs altitude (e.g., repeat Kohlhörster's measurements up to ~6000 m and beyond where possible), replicate in several geographic locations, and plan for international cooperation and resource pooling. Report measurement conditions, instrumentation, and altitude profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for hypotheses explaining stellar chromospheric emission differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanations for stronger chromospheric lines (H,K groups) in giant versus dwarf yellow stars should account for greater ionisation rates in giants, plausibly via an additional internal penetrating radiation or higher interior temperatures leading to dissociation and emission of penetrating rays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support such hypotheses with observational indicators (line strengths and widths compared to sun, relative brightness of chromospheric strata, spectral displacements like red/violet shifts in strata lines), theoretical estimates of interior temperatures and predicted high-frequency emission, and by considering alternative explanations (e.g., pressure effects, Saha ionisation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research prioritisation and justification for study of penetrating radiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Penetrating radiations are potentially key to understanding solar/stellar coronae, aurorae, magnetic disturbances, and nebular luminosity; their study is declared of high importance and urgency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing research programmes, justify resource allocation by linking anticipated measurements to multiple outstanding problems (aurorae, solar corona, nebulae). Outline concrete next steps (repeat ionisation-altitude surveys, laboratory analogues, international campaigns) and note expected costs and need for collaboration.
